newsitem.title: USA: Dow hits 5th record close in a row as rate worries ease.
newsitem.headline: Dow hits 5th record close in a row as rate worries ease.

text.p: Blue chip stocks roared to their fifth straight record finish on Thursday, riding a renewed wave of optimism on the outlook for stable interest rates.

The Dow Jones industrial average surged 135.64 points to end at a record 7,711.47 after surging over both the 7,600 and 7,700 hurdles for the first time. The index closed above 7,500 for the first time only on Tuesday, and ended at 7,575.83 on Wednesday.
In the broader market, advances outpaced declines 1,868 to 729 on volume of 592.7 million on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 3.47 points to 1,411.32.

The catalyst for the rally came directly from the bond market, where interest rates tumbled after the release of fresh data that suggested U.S. economic growth has moderated from a torrid first-quarter pace.

Analysts said the data, which included a surprising decline in U.S. retail sales over the last two months and a higher-than-expected level of weekly jobless claims, proved U.S. economic growth remains within the Federal Reserve's -- and therefore the market's -- comfort zone.

"The combination of those two numbers led people to believe the economy is decelerating and the Fed is on hold at its upcoming meeting," said Phil Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management. "This is Nirvana."

The speed of the rally, coupled with very heavy volume that approached 600 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange, left the impression that investors were almost tripping over themselves to join the advance.

"We now have all the fence-sitters jumping in," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "I had figured we'd pause at 7,500, but here we are two days later and 200 points higher."
Almost lost in the blistering buying spree were new caution signals on the outlook for semiconductor industry bellwether Intel Corp.
Intel shares fell 3-7/8 to 143-5/8 after several Wall Street firms lowered ratings or earnings estimates on the company. Intel also cut prices on its high-end MMX family of processors.

But in contrast to just two weeks ago, when an Intel warning about its near-term profit outlook stunned Wall Street and sent much of the market tumbling, investors this time largely brushed off the developments.
"That may have been the most bullish aspect of today's action," said Marshall Acuff, portfolio strategist at Smith Barney. "The market just shook it off and really roared."
Financial and cyclical stocks were among the strongest, although the rally was broadly based, with more than two stocks gaining for every one that fell.
BankAmerica Corp. rose 2-5/8 to 129-5/8, First Union Corp. gained 1-7/8 to 93-1/8 and Merrill Lynch & Co. jumped 1-3/8 to 59-3/4.
To be sure, the market faces a bit of a test Friday, with release of the May Producer Price Index, analysts said.
The report, a gauge of wholesale prices, has remained stubbornly low month after month, and economists are expecting a meagre 0.1 percent rise for May.

If prices rise more than expected, the market could fall into retreat, analysts said. On the other hand, a tame inflation report would provide yet another sign the economy is operating exactly the way investors like -- moderate growth without inflation.
"Right now, you ask 'What's wrong with this picture?' and you get silence," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany. "I just wonder how long it can last."
Among individual issues, Polo Ralph Lauren Corp. jumped 5-1/2 to 31-1/2 in the company's market debut after an initial public stock offering.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks rose 13.89 points to 883.46, a record. The American Stock Exchange index edged up 3.45 to 626.12.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 7.14 to 460.64, a record. The average price per share rose 69 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues also known as the Wilshire 5000 -- was a record 8,334.215, up 107.071, or 1.30 percent.
